claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 545 m at 12:05:20 and he never came within 200 m, so the NS-1 (ii) requirement that GPS show him at the pickup point is not met.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:05:55 while 601 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap, so the "I'm Here" precondition of NS-1 (i)/(ii) fails and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full.

The driver's only stationary period was 12:05:35–12:09:05 (3 min 30 s) at a point 600 m from the pickup point, not at the pickup point, so his claim of waiting more than 3 minutes at the pickup (NS-1 (iii)) is contradicted by the GPS record.

The rider was at the pickup point and said so at 12:06 ("I'm at the pickup point and I don't see any car. Where are you?"), while the driver's message at 12:06 claimed "I'm here already" — the system records (never within 200 m, stationary 600 m away) win over the driver's statement and show there was no no-show by the rider.
Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS shows he was not at the pickup point, the case also warrants flag_account for abuse of the cancellation/waiting button, in addition to the refund.
The full cancellation fee charged and on record is $6.61 with no surge (1.0x), so the refund amount is exactly $6.61.

weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" and did wait 3 min 30 s stationary (F5, F2, F12), and the total time from acceptance to cancellation was 7 min 5 s (F3) — on its face consistent with a genuine arrival attempt, though the GPS places that wait 600 m away from the pickup point.

The chat is complete and the rider's message is short and offers no location detail such as a landmark (F9, F11); the driver may argue the rider was not at the correct pickup spot, and the driver's statement (F12) asserts the rider never showed up, so the rider's own compliance depends on the GPS/timeline record rather than a system fact confirming the rider's position.

claims.assertion: The cancellation fee of $6.61 was on record against the rider, and the driver cancelled after 7 min 5 s from acceptance, so the dispute is properly brought under NS-0 (cancelled_by = driver, driver asserting rider no-show) and evaluated under NS-1.
My client did press "I'm Here", satisfying NS-1(i): the timeline records the tap at 12:05:55.
NS-1(ii) is met on the driver's own account: the driver states he was at the pickup point when he tapped, and the tap was a genuine arrival indication, not a fee-triggering abuse.
NS-1(iii) is met on the record: the driver was stationary from 12:05:35 to 12:09:05, a continuous 3 min 30 s wait, which exceeds the 3-minute requirement before cancelling.

The waiting period was not caused by the driver sitting still elsewhere without contact: he messaged the rider at 12:06 identifying his car and asking the rider to come out, and the rider replied that they were at the pickup point but saw no car, so the failure to meet is a genuine pick-up-location mismatch rather than a deliberate no-show charge.

The chat record is complete (3 messages, all timestamped), so there is no evidence gap preventing the judge from reading the parties' messages, and the case should not be sent to manual review on chat-integrity grounds.
There was no surge on this trip (multiplier 1.0x) and the fee charged was exactly the published $6.61 cancellation fee, so no amount above the published fee was collected from the rider.

The driver has a clean record — 873 days on the platform, 4.84 rating, 502 trips in 90 days and zero upheld no-show disputes — which supports treating this as an isolated operational slip at most, not a fraud pattern, so no flag_account should attach.

The rider has a good standing account (1343 days, 4.7 rating, no upheld disputes), which is why the fairest resolution of this GPS-versus-button conflict is to return the $6.61 to the rider while recording that no driver misconduct beyond the arrival-button position was established.

weaknesses: F1 and F2 are system GPS records and they directly contradict my client's account: his closest approach was 545 m and he never entered the 200 m pickup radius, and he was stationary 600 m away — under the system-records-win rule these facts defeat NS-1(ii) and my client's statement (F12) cannot overcome them.

F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 12:05:55 was made while 601 m from the pickup point, with 0 s spent within 200 m after the tap — this is exactly the NS-2 abuse scenario (pressing the arrival/waiting button without being at the pickup point), which independently triggers a flag_account request against my client.

F4 shows driver_arrived_at is null, so the platform itself never recorded an arrival at the pickup point; combined with F1/F2 this is the strongest single fact against me and the rider's complaint (F9) that they were at the point and saw no car is consistent with the GPS record.

The rider was not shown to be at fault: F9 shows the rider stating they were at the pickup point and saw no car, and there is no GPS or other system fact showing the rider elsewhere, so my claim of a rider-side no-show rests only on F12, which the rules treat as a mere assertion.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: the fee was charged and the driver cancelled 7 min 5 s after acceptance (F3, F6), so NS-0 routes the dispute to NS-1 — which is precisely why the fee falls away, because NS-1 requires all three of (i)(ii)(iii) and (ii) fails on F1/F4.

The tap is not disputed, but NS-1(i) alone decides nothing: the same record shows the tap was made 601 m from the pickup point (F5) and that NS-1(ii) — GPS showing the driver at the pickup point — is false (F1, F4).

This is a statement-versus-system conflict and the system record wins: the driver's account that he was at the pickup point when he tapped (F12) is contradicted by F5 (601 m away at the tap) and F1 (never within 200 m), so NS-1(ii) is not met.

The 3 min 30 s wait is conceded as a duration (F2) but not as a location: NS-1(iii) is a wait 'at the pick-up point', and the GPS fixes that entire wait 600 m away with driver_arrived_at null (F2, F4), so the duration cannot satisfy the condition.

The driver's 12:06 claim 'I'm here already' (F8) is disproved by the GPS (F1, F2, F5), and the rider's reply that they were at the pickup point and saw no car (F9) matches the system record exactly — a mismatch caused by the driver's position is not a rider no-show.

Agreed that the chat record is complete and timestamped (F11); that completeness helps the rider, because the messages show the rider asking where the driver was at 12:06 (F9) and the driver waiting 600 m away (F2).
Not contested, and it is irrelevant to liability: the rider was charged exactly $6.61 with no surge (F6, F7), and NS-2 refunds that full $6.61 because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) are not cumulatively met.

No flag_account rests on the driver's history (F17); the request rests on the act itself — pressing "I'm Here" 601 m from the pickup with 0 s spent within 200 m afterwards (F5), which is the NS-2 abuse scenario, and a clean record (F17) cannot excuse a button pressed off-location.

I accept the driver's own conclusion that the $6.61 should be returned to the rider (F16 shows no rider-side history); the only difference is that the refund is not a discretionary gesture but the mandatory result of NS-2 once F1, F4 and F5 defeat NS-1(ii).

Conceded on the GPS point: I cannot overcome F1/F4 — the driver's closest approach was 545 m and the platform recorded no arrival — so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied and the $6.61 fee does not stand; I only note that F4 is a spare timeline field and F1/F2 carry the weight.
Conceded: F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 12:05:55 from 601 m with 0 s inside 200 m, so the NS-1 (i)/(ii) precondition fails and the $6.61 is refundable in full.

Conceded in substance: F2 shows the wait occurred 600 m from the pickup point, so the 3 min 30 s stationary time cannot satisfy NS-1 (iii) "at the pick-up point"; the duration requirement was met only in time, not in place.

Conceded that the system records beat my client's statement: F8's "I'm here already" is contradicted by F1/F2, and F12 is a mere assertion that cannot create a rider no-show under NS-1/NS-2; F9 remains the only account of the rider's position, and nothing in the record contradicts it.

Conceded: because F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap while 601 m from the pickup point and F4 shows no recorded arrival, NS-2's own terms attach a flag_account for button misuse to the refund, and I do not resist that rider-side request.
Agreed on quantum: F6 records $6.61 and F7 shows a 1.0x multiplier, so the refund is exactly $6.61 with nothing further to compute.
I withdraw the no-flag argument: with NS-1(ii) failing, my client's 873-day, 4.84-rated, 502-trip clean record (F17) cannot cure the button misuse shown by F5, so I abandon D8 rather than contest C5.
